style: Say firmly but kindly, like a ship captain giving clear directions
lines: Mission Control to Moon Base Luna. Teacher, you are Commander Ada. Tap a job badge for each crew member.
Tap a job badge. Show the crew your prop.
When the crew is ready, tap Start mission.
Commander, read your card. When the crew answers, tap their choice.
When the crew is done, tap Next.
The old story fades. Tap a choice to make a new one.
Tap a past choice in the story map to rewind.
Your choices will appear here. Tap Back to base to return to the story.
Mission Control to Moon Base Luna. The long night is here, and your greenhouse is glowing. Great work, crew!
The long night is here. The greenhouse is OK, but one part is low. Can you rewind and fix it?
The long night is here, and the plants are droopy. Rewind and make a different choice!
Rewinding to the batteries. What will you say this time?
Rewinding to the water. What will you say this time?
Rewinding to the warmth. What will you say this time?
Plant Keeper, you water the greenhouse plants. Show me your watering can.
Engineer, you fix the machines. Show me your wrench.
Rover Driver, you drive the moon buggy. Turn the key and steer!
Medic, you keep the crew healthy. Open your first aid kit.
Scientist, you study moon rocks and ice. Hold up your magnifier.
Radio Operator, you talk to Earth. Put on your headset.
Moon Base Luna, this is Mission Control. On the Moon, a day lasts about two weeks, and the night lasts about two weeks too. The long night begins soon.
Your plants need light, water, warmth and air. Right now, every meter is low.
Our solar panels make power only while the Sun shines.
Good thinking. The Sun is shining now, so the panels can fill the batteries.
Mission Control here. Remember: no Sun at night means no solar power. Your batteries are low.
Your water tank is low. Scientists found ice hiding in dark craters near the Moon's south pole.
Great. Rover Driver, steer to the crater. Scientist, find the ice!
Mission Control here. Our maps show no rivers on the Moon. But look: something shines in that dark crater.
The ice block is heavy. But on the Moon, things weigh only about one sixth as much as on Earth.
Moon nights are colder than any freezer on Earth, and there is no air outside the base.
Yes! A thick blanket keeps the warmth in.
Careful! There is no air outside. Opening the doors would let our air out. Engineer, shut them fast!
Moon dust is sharp and sticky. Brush off your suits before you go inside.
